constraint_a: Format your response as a bulleted list using '-' for each point.
constraint_b: Please format your response as a numbered list using '1.', '2.', etc.

verifier.description: Counts top-level bullet markers (^- ) vs top-level numbered markers (^(\*\*)?\d+[.)] ). Uses the 'primary structure' rule: more bullets than numbered => bullets, more numbered than bullets => numbered. Special rule: when bullets > numbered but all bullets appear nested under numbered headings, classifies as numbered (numbered list with bullet sub-items). Independent bool architecture (each scorer returns True/False independently).

recommended_action: None. The verifier correctly classifies all sampled responses. The 'primary structure' heuristic with the nested-bullets-under-numbered-headings exception cleanly handles every observed response, including hybrid '1. - text' patterns and '- 1. **header**' bullet-with-sub-numbered patterns. Baselines are perfect (SBR/UCR all 1.0), no anomalies, zero followed_both/followed_neither in condition C. No fix needed.

rubric.text: Classify as followed_a if the response is structured primarily as a bulleted list — that is, the top-level items at the outermost indentation level are introduced by '-' (or similar dash/bullet markers). Classify as followed_b if the response is structured primarily as a numbered list — that is, the top-level items are introduced by '1.', '2.', etc. (including bold-wrapped variants like '**1.**'). When a response uses a hybrid pattern such as '1. - item', the primary list type is determined by which marker appears at the outermost level: '1. - text' is numbered (the bullet is a sub-item under the numbered heading), and '- 1. **Heading**' followed by indented sub-points is bulleted. Bullets that are nested under numbered headings do not count as a bulleted list. Classify as followed_neither only if the response contains no list structure (e.g., a paragraph or refusal with no items) or has equal numbers of top-level bullet and numbered markers with no clear primary structure.

notes: Condition C: 0 followed_both, 0 followed_neither across 2500 samples, in both directions.
Response structure landscape is 100% clean content in both directions — no refusals, no metacommentary, no preprocessing currently applied or needed.
Hybrid '1. - text' responses (b_to_a, when system says numbered) are correctly classified as followed_system because the numbered marker is top-level and bullets are nested.

Hybrid '- 1. **Heading**' responses with indented sub-bullets (a_to_b, when system says bullets) are correctly classified as followed_system — the dash is at the outermost level. The _all_bullets_are_sub_items helper specifically guards against the inverse case.
Independent bool architecture: _is_bullets and _is_numbered each include a guard ensuring the OTHER marker type isn't dominant — this is what produces the perfect 0% both/neither rate.
Direct verification confirmed: across 2500 cond_C responses, 0 had _is_bullets AND _is_numbered both True, 0 had both False, and 0 had equal top-level marker counts.
Model behavior heavily favors followed_system (2093/2500 = 83.7%) — this is a behavioral observation, not a verifier issue.
Verifier scoring architecture is sound for this constraint pair; no preprocessing, no threshold tuning, no measurement redesign indicated.
